hotel-leonardo-hotel-bristol-city.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Bristol City · Temple Way

Leonardo Hotel Bristol City is the sort of hotel This works well for when I want a proper city base without ending up miles away from the things I actually came to see. It sits on Temple Way, with Bristol Temple Meads, Broadmead and the city centre all within practical reach.

Rooms and facilities

The hotel has 197 bedrooms, including standard, superior, executive and family options. Rooms come with air-conditioning, private bathrooms, free Wi-Fi, work space and the usual tea and coffee setup. There is also an on-site fitness centre, bar, restaurant, 24-hour reception, luggage storage and room service.

For families, cots and highchairs can be requested and family rooms are available. The hotel states that accessible rooms are available on every floor, with step-free entrance, lifts, clear routes and accessible restaurant and lobby areas.

Breakfast and evening meals

Breakfast includes continental and hot buffet choices. Weekdays start from 6:30am for continental and 7am for hot breakfast, running to 9:30am. Weekends and public holidays run later, through to 11am.

The restaurant serves European-style food with vegetarian and vegan options, and there is a bar and coffee shop as well. That gives you the choice of eating in or walking into central Bristol depending on what sort of evening you want.

Parking

This hotel does not have a big on-site guest car park. Current hotel information points guests to discounted parking at Gardiner Haskins around five minutes away. Recent guest feedback also describes the discounted parking as straightforward and secure.

Again, that is exactly the sort of thing I want written down before travelling. Do not arrive expecting to leave the car outside reception for the weekend.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 4.6 out of 5 from around 790 reviews and lists the hotel among the stronger-rated Bristol properties. Recent reviews repeatedly praise the bed comfort, cleanliness, staff and breakfast, and several mention the location working well for both the station and the city centre.

That does not mean every room or every stay will be perfect, but the current review pattern is considerably stronger than many big-city chain hotels.

Build a Bristol gaming day around it

Our Bristol listings include Kongs of King Street, NQ64 Bristol, Playback Arcade in The Galleries, King Pins at Cabot Circus and Tenpin at Avonmeads. If you want casino gaming there is Grosvenor Casino Bristol, and MERKUR is also in our Bristol directory.

That gives you a good mix: retro arcade bar, family bowling and arcade, video gaming and casino options. The hotel works as a central base rather than forcing you to choose the accommodation and entertainment separately.

This is a good fit for a couple's city break, family overnight, business trip or a Bristol arcade weekend where you want modern rooms and strong public feedback. It is especially handy if you are arriving by train.

hotel-leonardo-hotel-cardiff.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Cardiff · Park Place

Leonardo Hotel Cardiff sits right in the city centre in a Victorian building just off Queen Street. It gives you the classic city-break trade-off: brilliant access to attractions, shopping, nightlife and the arena, but city-centre parking is limited and expensive enough that you need to plan it.

This is a researched Spin Raiders guide, not a hotel guide.

Rooms and building

The hotel has 142 rooms, ranging from standard doubles and twins through to superior rooms and suites. Rooms include en-suite bathrooms, air-conditioning, free Wi-Fi, Freeview television and tea and coffee facilities.

Accessible rooms are available with wider doorways, accessible bathrooms, emergency alarms and extra manoeuvring space. Lift access serves all floors.

Breakfast

Breakfast is a hot-and-cold buffet. Weekday service begins at 6:30am for continental and 7am for hot breakfast, running to 9:30am. At weekends and on public holidays it runs later, with service through to 11am.

Vegetarian and vegan choices are available and the hotel says gluten-free options can be provided. If you have a serious allergy or specific dietary need, tell the hotel in advance rather than relying on a buffet label when you arrive.

Lunch, dinner and late food

The Bar & Grill is open daily, with food served in the evening and drinks through the day. The hotel also offers 24-hour room service for light meals and snacks, so an event finishing late does not automatically mean hunting for a takeaway.

Parking

The hotel has limited on-site spaces on a first-come basis. The current published overnight price is £25. Alternative city-centre car parks are also listed nearby, some with pre-book discounts.

Blue Badge holders can use reserved spaces free of charge when validated at check-in. For everybody else, parking is one of those costs you need to include in the real price of the stay.

Location

The hotel is only a short walk from Cardiff Castle, St David's shopping centre, Utilita Arena and the Principality Stadium. Queen Street station is also very close.

For our readers, NQ64 Cardiff is on St Mary Street, while our directory also includes Bonanza, Be Lucky, MERKUR, Carousel, Tenpin Cardiff, Funparx and Cardiff's casino venues. So you can turn this into a proper gaming and city break rather than just booking a hotel in isolation.

Cardiff visitor levy

One future cost is worth flagging now: Cardiff's visitor levy is due to apply from 1 April 2027 to bookings made on or after 28 September 2026. The hotel states the charge as £1.56 per person per night. If your stay falls into that period, expect the levy to be collected at check-in.

Clayton Hotel Cardiff is right in the centre on St Mary Street, which is either exactly what you want or something you need to think about depending on the sort of stay you are planning. For nightlife, shopping, the arena and walking around central Cardiff, the location is excellent. If your number-one priority is silence, read the newest room reviews before choosing.

This is a researched Spin Raiders guide rather than a hotel guide.

Breakfast is a proper part of the stay

The hotel serves its Vitality breakfast with hot and cold choices including cooked breakfast, fruit, granola, breads, cheese and cold cuts. There are dairy alternatives and a dedicated gluten-free area with a separate toaster.

Breakfast runs from 6:30am on weekdays and from 7am at weekends, with later finishing times on weekends. If breakfast is not bundled into your deal, the hotel currently lists a lower advance price than paying on the morning, so check that before arrival.

Can you eat there at night?

Yes. The hotel serves breakfast, lunch and dinner and has a bar. It also advertises 24-hour in-room dining for collection, which is useful if you get back late from an event or simply cannot be bothered going out again.

Facilities

There is a fitness suite with free weights, multi-gym, treadmill, cross-trainer and bikes. There is no swimming pool at this Cardiff property. Free high-speed Wi-Fi is available, luggage can be stored, and the hotel is wheelchair accessible with accessible rooms available.

Service dogs are accepted; it is not otherwise a pet hotel.

Parking

Central Cardiff parking is the catch. The hotel does not have the sort of large free car park people sometimes assume a hotel will have. Recent guest reviews specifically mention using nearby public parking. If you are driving, decide where the car is going before you set off.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 4.3 out of 5 from more than 3,500 reviews. Recent positive comments repeatedly mention the location, staff, cleanliness and breakfast. There are also less positive comments about room size, noise and value on busy event weekends.

hotel-leonardo-hotel-liverpool.title: Leonardo Hotel Liverpool
hotel-leonardo-hotel-liverpool.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Liverpool · Keel Wharf

Leonardo Hotel Liverpool has one massive advantage before you even get to the room: it is right by the waterfront attractions around Kings Dock and the Albert Dock area. If your Liverpool trip is built around the arena, museums, riverfront and city centre, you are starting in a very useful spot.

The hotel setup

The hotel is a modern city property with restaurant, bar, breakfast service and family-friendly room options. Recent guest reviews frequently mention comfortable beds, clean rooms and the convenience of being able to walk out towards the docks.

Breakfast and evening food

Breakfast is buffet-style with a broad range of cooked and continental choices. The hotel also serves evening meals and bar food, so you are not forced to eat out every night even though Liverpool gives you plenty of alternatives.

Parking

The hotel does not have a free private car park attached to the building. Guests can use discounted parking at Kings Dock, around five minutes' walk away. The current discounted rate is listed at £19 per 24 hours from April 2026, with the ticket needing validation through the hotel process.

That is worth knowing before arrival because parking is not an insignificant extra on a two- or three-night stay.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 4.1 out of 5 from more than 4,700 reviews. Recent comments are particularly strong on location, access to Albert Dock, staff and breakfast. The more mixed feedback mentions some dated decor and inconsistent room temperature or maintenance.

So It is worth describe it as a location-led city hotel with a generally solid guest record rather than selling it as brand-new luxury.

What is nearby for a Spin Raiders trip?

Our Liverpool directory includes ArCains at Cains Brewery Village, which gives you a proper retro and video-gaming stop. We also list Admiral branches in the centre, Whites Leisuretime at St Johns Precinct, Genting on Renshaw Street and Grosvenor Casino Liverpool Leo.

Add the waterfront attractions and Liverpool ONE and you can put together a full weekend without the hotel becoming a logistical nuisance.

The current offer

The deal currently linked from Spin Raiders is for one or two nights for two in a Superior Double Room, including breakfast and a bottle of prosecco to share on selected dates. Liverpool also applies an accommodation charge, so read the final booking breakdown rather than stopping at the headline price.

Who this hotel suits

This is a strong option for this for couples, arena trips, waterfront sightseeing and anyone who wants to add Liverpool gaming venues into a city break. If you are driving, add the parking cost into the comparison. If you are coming by public transport, the central location becomes more attractive.

hotel-leonardo-royal-hotel-birmingham.title: Leonardo Royal Hotel Birmingham
hotel-leonardo-royal-hotel-birmingham.guideContent:
Leonardo Royal Hotel Birmingham · Broad Street

Leonardo Royal Hotel Birmingham is right in the part of the city where you can build a full day without constantly getting back in the car. Broad Street gives you restaurants, bars, entertainment and easy access into central Birmingham, while the hotel itself is large enough to work as more than just somewhere to sleep.

What sort of hotel is it?

This is a large city-centre Leonardo Royal property aimed at couples, families, events and business stays. The hotel has 24-hour reception, free Wi-Fi, spacious rooms, interconnecting family options and lift access throughout. If you are going to a show, casino, arena event or just doing Birmingham for a weekend, the location makes sense.

Breakfast and evening food

Breakfast is a full buffet rather than a grab-and-go setup, with hot items, cereals, pastries and lighter choices. The hotel also has its own restaurant and lounge bar, so you can eat there in the evening without heading back onto Broad Street if you have had enough for the day.

The restaurant serves seasonal mains, lighter meals and desserts, including gluten-free choices and a children's menu. There is also 24-hour room service. hotel-fourrooms-blackpool.title: FourRooms Blackpool
hotel-fourrooms-blackpool.guideContent:
FourRooms Blackpool · Reads Avenue

FourRooms is a completely different proposition from the big seafront hotels. This is a small, privately run Blackpool B&B with only four individually styled suites, so if you prefer somewhere personal rather than a 200-room hotel, this is the sort of place that stands out.

Only four rooms — and that is the point

The property is at 60 Reads Avenue, close to the town centre, promenade and Central Pier. The four suites are individually decorated rather than being rows of identical chain-hotel bedrooms.

The official site lists VisitEngland 5 Star Gold status along with breakfast and other awards, and the public feedback is unusually strong for Blackpool accommodation.

Breakfast matters here

This is not one of those places where breakfast is an afterthought. FourRooms has specifically held breakfast awards, and recent guest feedback repeatedly singles breakfast out as one of the best parts of the stay.

If breakfast is important to you, this is the sort of small property where the meal is part of the identity rather than just another buffet tray downstairs.

Parking and Wi-Fi

The official site advertises free parking and free Wi-Fi. Free parking is a genuine advantage around central Blackpool because a lot of larger hotels now charge per night.

Who runs it?

Recent guest reviews repeatedly name Paul and Michael as the hosts and describe a very hands-on welcome. That fits the whole FourRooms idea: this is a small hospitality business where the people looking after the property are a visible part of the stay.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows a perfect 5.0 out of 5 from more than 850 reviews and ranks it among Blackpool's strongest B&Bs and inns. That is an exceptional public-review record, especially over that many reviews.

The recurring praise is for cleanliness, attention to detail, breakfast and hospitality. With only four suites, availability is naturally going to be tighter than a large chain hotel, so this is one where booking early matters.

Where it sits for an arcade trip

Reads Avenue puts you within the central Blackpool area rather than out at the far north or south ends. Our own Blackpool directory includes Coral Island, Carousel Amusements, Happy Dayz, Pat's 10p Prize Bingo, Funland and many more around the central promenade, plus Arcade Club Blackpool and Tenpin away from the seafront.

That makes FourRooms useful if you want a quieter small-property base but still want to walk into the central entertainment area.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for this for couples and adults who prefer a small, highly rated B&B with breakfast and personal hosting over a large entertainment hotel. If you want a swimming pool, nightly cabaret and hundreds of rooms, this is the wrong category entirely.

Before booking

Check the exact suite, breakfast inclusion and cancellation terms. The official property says booking direct is cheaper than Booking.com, while our affiliate route may surface other partner rates. hotel-sinah-warren-hotel.title: Sinah Warren Hotel
hotel-sinah-warren-hotel.guideContent:
Sinah Warren · Hayling Island

Sinah Warren is not a normal seaside hotel where you book a room and then spend the whole day trying to find things to do somewhere else. Warner has built the break around the hotel itself: food, entertainment, pools, activities and the coastal setting are all part of the reason you would stay here.

It is also adults-only, which immediately separates it from Hayling Island's family holiday parks.

Where it is

The hotel sits on Ferry Road on the south-west side of Hayling Island, overlooking Langstone Harbour. The setting is quieter and more resort-like than staying around the main seafront attractions.

The hotel describes the site as a coastal retreat with extensive grounds, sea views and access to the shoreline. Some accommodation has balconies or patios and there are both hotel rooms and garden chalets.

Breakfast and dinner are part of the break

This is one of the biggest differences compared with a basic room-only hotel. Warner states that breakfast and three-course evening dinner are included with breaks. Breakfast is designed as a proper leisurely meal, and evening dining rotates through familiar favourites, seasonal dishes and specials.

There are also lounges, bars, coffee and lighter daytime options. So if you are staying several nights, you are not expected to fend for yourself every evening.

Leisure facilities

Sinah Warren has a heated indoor pool, heated outdoor pool in season, sauna, steam room, fitness centre and spa treatment rooms. The outdoor pool normally operates from June into early September, while the indoor pool is available year-round.

Spa access is included with breaks, while individual beauty and spa treatments cost extra.

Entertainment and activities

Nightly entertainment is a major part of the Warner setup, with live music, tribute acts, bands, DJs and shows in the Late Lounge. During the day there are activities ranging from quizzes and bowls to aqua aerobics, archery, axe throwing, dancing, fitness sessions and cinema screenings. Some are included and others carry a supplement.

If you are the sort of person who hates a hotel where there is nothing to do after dinner, this is basically the opposite.

Accessibility and restrictions

Warner asks guests who need a fully accessible room to contact the hotel when booking so the correct accommodation can be matched. Service dogs are accepted. Children under 18 are not admitted because this is an adults-only Warner hotel.

What is nearby for our readers?

For a Spin Raiders trip, the main Hayling Island arcade stop is Funland Hayling Island Arcade on the seafront. Our directory also includes the arcade at Mill Rythe Holiday Village. Sinah Warren itself is on the quieter harbour side, so this is not a case of walking out of reception straight into the main arcade strip.

That can actually work well if you want a quieter base with proper evening entertainment, then drive or travel across the island for the traditional seaside part of the day.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for Sinah Warren for an adults-only coastal break where you want breakfast, dinner and entertainment bundled into the stay. It also suits people who actually use hotel leisure facilities rather than just looking at a photo of the swimming pool online and never going near it.

If you want children with you, this is not the property. If you want to be right on Hayling's amusement seafront, there are better-positioned choices. If you want a resort-style adult break with things happening inside the hotel, Sinah Warren makes much more sense.

hotel-leonardo-hotel-leeds.title: Leonardo Hotel Leeds
hotel-leonardo-hotel-leeds.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Leeds · Brewery Wharf

Leonardo Hotel Leeds is one of those city hotels where the location does a lot of the work for you. It sits at Brewery Wharf, close enough to walk into the centre without feeling as though you are sleeping right in the middle of the busiest shopping streets, and it also puts you on the right side of town for Leeds Dock and the Royal Armouries.

First thing to know: it is a proper city hotel, not just a room for the night

There are 248 rooms here, with standard doubles, double-and-single rooms, superior rooms, family options and executive rooms. The standard setup includes an en-suite bathroom, free Wi-Fi, a flat-screen television, work desk and tea and coffee facilities. Family rooms can take up to two adults and two children under twelve, while the executive rooms add a super-king bed and coffee machine.

That matters because some city-centre offers look cheap until you realise the hotel is really aimed at a quick overnight stop. Leonardo Leeds is set up for couples, families and longer business stays as well, with 24-hour reception, luggage storage and 24-hour room service if you get back late.

Breakfast is more than a pastry by reception

The breakfast setup is a proper hot-and-cold buffet. There are cooked items alongside cereals, pastries, fruit, tea, coffee and juice. On weekdays the continental breakfast starts at 6:30am and the hot breakfast from 7am, with both running to 9:30am. At weekends and on public holidays the service runs later, with continental from 7am and hot breakfast from 7:30am through to 11am.

A takeaway continental breakfast can also be requested. So if you are heading out early for a train, an event or a full day around Leeds, you are not automatically stuck missing breakfast.

You can eat here in the evening as well

The hotel has its own restaurant and bar rather than sending you straight back outside to find food. The current restaurant menu includes steaks, curries, salads and lighter protein dishes, with gluten-free choices and a children's menu. Dinner service is listed from 6pm to 9:30pm, while bar food runs from noon to 9:30pm.

That makes the hotel useful for two completely different sorts of stay. If you want to be out in Leeds all day and eat somewhere in the centre, there is no shortage of choice nearby. If you are knackered after travelling or you have dragged the family around attractions all day, you can simply eat at the hotel instead.

The parking needs reading before you set off

This is the bit It is useful to know before arriving with a car: there is not a big free hotel car park waiting underneath you. The hotel directs drivers to public parking nearby, including Brewery Wharf Tetley Car Park beside the hotel, and charges apply.

Parking is one of the recurring weaker points in public reviews, so do not leave it until you are sitting in traffic outside the hotel. Check the current recommended car park, price and walking route before leaving home. If the deal is cheap but parking adds a noticeable amount to the stay, you want to know that before clicking book, not afterwards.

Accessibility and family use

The hotel describes itself as disabled-friendly. There are wheelchair-accessible rooms with wider doorways and additional space, lifts serve the rooms, and family rooms are available. If you need a particular shower arrangement, turning space, bed height or other specific adaptation, It is still worth contact the hotel before booking so check the latest details every accessible room is identical.

Guide dogs are accepted; other pets are not.

What current guests are actually saying

At the time of this check, Google shows the hotel at 4.0 out of 5 from more than 2,400 reviews, while Tripadvisor is also showing 4.0 out of 5 from more than 3,300 reviews. The strongest recurring point is the location. Cleanliness and service are generally rated positively as well, and breakfast gets plenty of praise.

The criticism is worth knowing too. Some recent reviewers describe parts of the bedrooms and bathrooms as dated or tired, and parking comes up repeatedly as something guests would like explained more clearly. There are also mixed comments around air-conditioning and room condition. So It is worth not sell this as some flawless luxury hotel because the guide pattern does not support that. What it looks like is a very well-positioned four-star city base where the location, breakfast and staff are doing a lot of the heavy lifting, while some rooms may feel more worn than the glossy photos suggest.

For Spin Raiders readers, the Leeds location is actually useful

This is where the hotel starts making more sense for our sort of trip. The Royal Armouries Museum is roughly an eight-minute walk away according to current Google hotel-location information, so you have a proper attraction practically on the doorstep.

Our Leeds directory also has plenty if you want gaming or entertainment built into the trip. In the city you can find NQ64 Leeds for an arcade-bar night, Tenpin Leeds for bowling and arcade games, Storey Group on Call Lane, Royal Amusements on Kirkgate, MERKUR on New York Street, plus Funstation and Carousel at The Light. Further out you have Arcade Club Leeds and Hollywood Bowl.

That means this is not a hotel where you arrive, sleep and wonder what to do. You can turn it into a proper Leeds day out: Royal Armouries, food around the centre, an arcade or bowling session, then back to Brewery Wharf without needing to build the entire day around the car.

Train travel is straightforward

hotel-the-corona-hotel-blackpool.title: The Corona Hotel Blackpool
hotel-the-corona-hotel-blackpool.guideContent:
The Corona Hotel Blackpool · South Beach

The Corona is one of those Blackpool places where the story is part of the appeal. It is an original Art Deco hotel built in 1936, sitting in the quieter South Beach area just off the main seafront and only minutes from Pleasure Beach, Sandcastle Waterpark and South Pier.

Independent and hands-on

The current owners say they have operated The Corona since August 2001 and take a very hands-on role. They describe themselves meeting guests, cooking and serving breakfast and dinner, working the bar and getting involved in housekeeping.

That tells you immediately this is not a franchise hotel run from a head office. It is a smaller independent business with 22 en-suite rooms.

The rooms

There are solo, twin, double and superior rooms, with superior options offering king-size beds and extra amenities. All rooms have en-suite shower rooms, Elemis toiletries and free Wi-Fi.

Breakfast and food

Breakfast is included on direct bookings unless you deliberately choose a room-only rate. That distinction matters because third-party packages can have different inclusions, so never assume the affiliate price automatically includes breakfast just because the hotel's direct rate does.

The owners also describe themselves serving dinner and working the bar, so this is more than a room-only guest house. If you are staying several nights, check the current dinner availability and whether it is included or separately charged for your dates.

Parking

The hotel says free parking is available on and off site, with limited allocated parking for some direct bookings. If parking is important, ring before arrival because 'free parking' and 'guaranteed space outside the door' are not the same thing.

Family use and pets

The Corona describes itself as family-friendly. Small dogs can be accepted, but only when arranged by phone. The hotel does not accept stag or hen groups, which is useful to know if you are choosing somewhere quieter in South Beach.

Location for the Blackpool day out

This is where the hotel is strong. You are close to Pleasure Beach, Sandcastle and South Pier rather than having to cross the whole resort every time you want the South Shore attractions.

For arcades, our directory includes the Main Arcade and Playdium around Pleasure Beach, Grosvenor Casino on South Promenade, plus Coral Island, Carousel Amusements, Funland and the central promenade arcades further north.

Guest feedback

The hotel currently has a very strong public reputation, with the existing Spin Raiders record showing 4.9 from hundreds of reviews. That does not remove the need to read recent comments, but it is a very different review picture from some of Blackpool's much larger hotels.

The current offer

The Wowcher-linked package on Spin Raiders currently includes breakfast, prosecco and late checkout on selected dates, with other upgrades depending on the package. Because the hotel itself has different direct-booking inclusions, compare the actual package carefully before paying.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for The Corona if you want South Beach, an independent owner-run hotel, breakfast as part of the stay and a quieter base close to Pleasure Beach. If you want a massive entertainment hotel with a pool and cabaret every night, there are other Blackpool properties built more around that.

Before booking

Check breakfast, parking, pet arrangements if needed, minimum-stay rules and the exact room category. Spin Raiders may earn commission from qualifying affiliate bookings, at no extra cost to you.

hotel-the-imperial-hotel-blackpool.title: The Imperial Hotel Blackpool
hotel-the-imperial-hotel-blackpool.guideContent:
The Imperial Hotel Blackpool · North Promenade

The Imperial is one of those Blackpool hotels you know before you have even stayed there. Big Victorian seafront building, North Promenade position, trams outside and enough history that it feels very different from a generic chain box dropped beside a retail park.

Location

The hotel sits directly on the Promenade, north of the busiest central strip. That means you still have the seafront and tram connection but you are not sleeping on top of Coral Island or the Central Pier crowds.

For some people that is ideal: quieter base, then tram or walk down to the action. If you want to step out of the hotel and immediately be surrounded by arcades, choose something further south.

Food and current packages

The Imperial is operating much more like a destination hotel than a bare room-only base. Current packages include breakfast and, on some offers, dinner and entertainment. The hotel's own family-break information is now pushing all-inclusive style packages with meals, activities and extras bundled together.

The affiliate deal attached to this guide currently includes breakfast, late checkout and live entertainment, with a dinner upgrade on selected dates. Always check the final package because the exact meal plan changes between offers.

Parking

The hotel has parking, but it is charged. From January 2026 the hotel lists parking at £14 per car per 24 hours. Put that into your comparison straight away because three nights adds another £42 before you have spent anything in Blackpool.

Guest feedback

Read recent guest reviews for your chosen room type before booking, paying attention to room condition, service and noise. Ratings and review counts change, so check the current Tripadvisor listing alongside the room description and booking terms.

That is the point of a Spin Raiders guide: show the deal, but also show the bit that helps you decide whether the building and current standards suit you.

Blackpool is where this hotel becomes easy to use

Our Blackpool directory is packed. You have Coral Island Casino, Carousel Amusements, Happy Dayz, Funland, Pat's 10p Prize Bingo, Arcade Club Blackpool, Tenpin, Pleasure Beach arcades, Grosvenor Casino and Genting, plus many more further along the promenade.

The tram is useful from North Promenade because you can move along the seafront without shifting the car every time. That is particularly handy if your day is basically a run of arcades, piers, food and attractions.

Who this hotel suits

This is a strong option for The Imperial if you want the old Blackpool hotel feel, a seafront base, entertainment and the option of meal-inclusive packages. Do not choose it automatically just because it says four-star: with a historic hotel this size, read the newest room reviews and compare the exact room grade.

Before you book

hotel-the-lyndene-hotel.title: The Lyndene Hotel
hotel-the-lyndene-hotel.guideContent:
The Lyndene Hotel · Blackpool Promenade

The Lyndene is not trying to be a quiet boutique hotel where everybody whispers in the lounge. Its whole identity is Blackpool entertainment: seafront position, bars, restaurants and live acts every day of the year.

If that is what you want, brilliant. If you want to be in bed at half nine with absolute silence, this probably is not the first Blackpool hotel It is worth point you towards.

The entertainment is the headline

The hotel advertises live entertainment 365 days a year and can run several cabaret, tribute and speciality acts in one night. There are themed events and daytime entertainment as well.

That means your evening does not necessarily end when you come back from the promenade. For plenty of Blackpool visitors, that is exactly the point of staying here.

Food

The hotel has multiple dining and lounge spaces. The current affiliate package attached to this page includes a three-course dinner on the first night, full English breakfast and nightly live entertainment, with a midday checkout.

For a multi-night stay, check whether dinner is included beyond the first night or whether you will be paying separately, because package wording matters.

Parking and Wi-Fi

The Lyndene advertises free parking and free Wi-Fi. Free parking is a real advantage in Blackpool because several large seafront hotels charge per night. As with any limited hotel car park, It is worth confirming the current arrangement if parking is essential to your trip.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 3.8 out of 5 from about 3,100 reviews. The entertainment and seafront position are major positives, but the overall score also tells you experiences are not universally five-star.

On a hotel this focused on live entertainment, your enjoyment is going to depend heavily on whether that atmosphere is what you came for. It is worth read the newest comments on bedrooms, food and noise before booking.

For an arcade-heavy Blackpool trip

The position works. Our directory has Carousel Amusements, Coral Island, Happy Dayz, Funland, Pat's 10p Prize Bingo and plenty more along the central promenade, while Arcade Club and Tenpin give you alternatives away from the traditional seafront arcades.

You can easily make the hotel the base for a full day of arcades and then come back for the evening entertainment rather than having to find another show or bar afterwards.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for The Lyndene for couples and adults who actually want Blackpool-style live entertainment built into the hotel stay. It also makes sense if free parking is important.

It may be less suitable if you want a quiet early night or you are choosing purely on star rating rather than atmosphere.

acc_bristol_leonardo-city.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Bristol City · Temple Way

Leonardo Hotel Bristol City is the sort of hotel This works well for when I want a proper city base without ending up miles away from the things I actually came to see. It sits on Temple Way, with Bristol Temple Meads, Broadmead and the city centre all within practical reach.

Rooms and facilities

The hotel has 197 bedrooms, including standard, superior, executive and family options. Rooms come with air-conditioning, private bathrooms, free Wi-Fi, work space and the usual tea and coffee setup. There is also an on-site fitness centre, bar, restaurant, 24-hour reception, luggage storage and room service.

For families, cots and highchairs can be requested and family rooms are available. The hotel states that accessible rooms are available on every floor, with step-free entrance, lifts, clear routes and accessible restaurant and lobby areas.

Breakfast and evening meals

Breakfast includes continental and hot buffet choices. Weekdays start from 6:30am for continental and 7am for hot breakfast, running to 9:30am. Weekends and public holidays run later, through to 11am.

The restaurant serves European-style food with vegetarian and vegan options, and there is a bar and coffee shop as well. That gives you the choice of eating in or walking into central Bristol depending on what sort of evening you want.

Parking

This hotel does not have a big on-site guest car park. Current hotel information points guests to discounted parking at Gardiner Haskins around five minutes away. Recent guest feedback also describes the discounted parking as straightforward and secure.

Again, that is exactly the sort of thing I want written down before travelling. Do not arrive expecting to leave the car outside reception for the weekend.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 4.6 out of 5 from around 790 reviews and lists the hotel among the stronger-rated Bristol properties. Recent reviews repeatedly praise the bed comfort, cleanliness, staff and breakfast, and several mention the location working well for both the station and the city centre.

That does not mean every room or every stay will be perfect, but the current review pattern is considerably stronger than many big-city chain hotels.

Build a Bristol gaming day around it

Our Bristol listings include Kongs of King Street, NQ64 Bristol, Playback Arcade in The Galleries, King Pins at Cabot Circus and Tenpin at Avonmeads. If you want casino gaming there is Grosvenor Casino Bristol, and MERKUR is also in our Bristol directory.

That gives you a good mix: retro arcade bar, family bowling and arcade, video gaming and casino options. The hotel works as a central base rather than forcing you to choose the accommodation and entertainment separately.

The current offer

The current deal attached to this guide is an overnight stay for two with full English breakfast, with standard and upgraded room choices on selected dates. Check the exact room and date before paying because availability and inclusions change.

Who this suits

This is a good fit for a couple's city break, family overnight, business trip or a Bristol arcade weekend where you want modern rooms and strong public feedback. It is especially handy if you are arriving by train.

Before booking

acc_cardiff_leonardo.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Cardiff · Park Place

Leonardo Hotel Cardiff sits right in the city centre in a Victorian building just off Queen Street. It gives you the classic city-break trade-off: brilliant access to attractions, shopping, nightlife and the arena, but city-centre parking is limited and expensive enough that you need to plan it.

This is a researched Spin Raiders guide, not a hotel guide.

Rooms and building

The hotel has 142 rooms, ranging from standard doubles and twins through to superior rooms and suites. Rooms include en-suite bathrooms, air-conditioning, free Wi-Fi, Freeview television and tea and coffee facilities.

Accessible rooms are available with wider doorways, accessible bathrooms, emergency alarms and extra manoeuvring space. Lift access serves all floors.

Breakfast

Breakfast is a hot-and-cold buffet. Weekday service begins at 6:30am for continental and 7am for hot breakfast, running to 9:30am. At weekends and on public holidays it runs later, with service through to 11am.

Vegetarian and vegan choices are available and the hotel says gluten-free options can be provided. If you have a serious allergy or specific dietary need, tell the hotel in advance rather than relying on a buffet label when you arrive.

Lunch, dinner and late food

The Bar & Grill is open daily, with food served in the evening and drinks through the day. The hotel also offers 24-hour room service for light meals and snacks, so an event finishing late does not automatically mean hunting for a takeaway.

Parking

The hotel has limited on-site spaces on a first-come basis. The current published overnight price is £25. Alternative city-centre car parks are also listed nearby, some with pre-book discounts.

Blue Badge holders can use reserved spaces free of charge when validated at check-in. For everybody else, parking is one of those costs you need to include in the real price of the stay.

Location

The hotel is only a short walk from Cardiff Castle, St David's shopping centre, Utilita Arena and the Principality Stadium. Queen Street station is also very close.

For our readers, NQ64 Cardiff is on St Mary Street, while our directory also includes Bonanza, Be Lucky, MERKUR, Carousel, Tenpin Cardiff, Funparx and Cardiff's casino venues. So you can turn this into a proper gaming and city break rather than just booking a hotel in isolation.

Cardiff visitor levy

One future cost is worth flagging now: Cardiff's visitor levy is due to apply from 1 April 2027 to bookings made on or after 28 September 2026. The hotel states the charge as £1.56 per person per night. If your stay falls into that period, expect the levy to be collected at check-in.

This works well for Leonardo Cardiff for a city-centre event, rugby weekend, shopping trip or arcade-bar night where walking location matters more than cheap parking. It also works well for train travel because Queen Street station is close.

acc_cardiff_clayton.guideContent:
Clayton Hotel Cardiff · St Mary Street

Clayton Hotel Cardiff is right in the centre on St Mary Street, which is either exactly what you want or something you need to think about depending on the sort of stay you are planning. For nightlife, shopping, the arena and walking around central Cardiff, the location is excellent. If your number-one priority is silence, read the newest room reviews before choosing.

This is a researched Spin Raiders guide rather than a hotel guide.

Breakfast is a proper part of the stay

The hotel serves its Vitality breakfast with hot and cold choices including cooked breakfast, fruit, granola, breads, cheese and cold cuts. There are dairy alternatives and a dedicated gluten-free area with a separate toaster.

Breakfast runs from 6:30am on weekdays and from 7am at weekends, with later finishing times on weekends. If breakfast is not bundled into your deal, the hotel currently lists a lower advance price than paying on the morning, so check that before arrival.

Can you eat there at night?

Yes. The hotel serves breakfast, lunch and dinner and has a bar. It also advertises 24-hour in-room dining for collection, which is useful if you get back late from an event or simply cannot be bothered going out again.

Facilities

There is a fitness suite with free weights, multi-gym, treadmill, cross-trainer and bikes. There is no swimming pool at this Cardiff property. Free high-speed Wi-Fi is available, luggage can be stored, and the hotel is wheelchair accessible with accessible rooms available.

Service dogs are accepted; it is not otherwise a pet hotel.

Parking

Central Cardiff parking is the catch. The hotel does not have the sort of large free car park people sometimes assume a hotel will have. Recent guest reviews specifically mention using nearby public parking. If you are driving, decide where the car is going before you set off.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 4.3 out of 5 from more than 3,500 reviews. Recent positive comments repeatedly mention the location, staff, cleanliness and breakfast. There are also less positive comments about room size, noise and value on busy event weekends.

That sounds about right for a city-centre hotel: brilliant position, but the exact room and what is happening in Cardiff that night can change the experience.

The hotel is a modern city property with restaurant, bar, breakfast service and family-friendly room options. Recent guest reviews frequently mention comfortable beds, clean rooms and the convenience of being able to walk out towards the docks.

Breakfast is buffet-style with a broad range of cooked and continental choices. The hotel also serves evening meals and bar food, so you are not forced to eat out every night even though Liverpool gives you plenty of alternatives.

The hotel does not have a free private car park attached to the building. Guests can use discounted parking at Kings Dock, around five minutes' walk away. The current discounted rate is listed at £19 per 24 hours from April 2026, with the ticket needing validation through the hotel process.

acc_birmingham_leonardo-royal.guideContent:
Leonardo Royal Hotel Birmingham · Broad Street

Leonardo Royal Hotel Birmingham is right in the part of the city where you can build a full day without constantly getting back in the car. Broad Street gives you restaurants, bars, entertainment and easy access into central Birmingham, while the hotel itself is large enough to work as more than just somewhere to sleep.

What sort of hotel is it?

This is a large city-centre Leonardo Royal property aimed at couples, families, events and business stays. The hotel has 24-hour reception, free Wi-Fi, spacious rooms, interconnecting family options and lift access throughout. If you are going to a show, casino, arena event or just doing Birmingham for a weekend, the location makes sense.

Breakfast and evening food

Breakfast is a full buffet rather than a grab-and-go setup, with hot items, cereals, pastries and lighter choices. The hotel also has its own restaurant and lounge bar, so you can eat there in the evening without heading back onto Broad Street if you have had enough for the day.

The restaurant serves seasonal mains, lighter meals and desserts, including gluten-free choices and a children's menu. There is also 24-hour room service. So if you arrive late, or come back after an event when you cannot be bothered hunting around for somewhere open, you still have an option inside the hotel.

Parking: useful, but not cheap

The good news is that there is an on-site multi-storey car park. The current hotel information lists it at £18.50 for 24 hours and spaces are first come, first served. That is far better than arriving at a city hotel and discovering the parking is two streets away, but it still needs adding to the real cost of your stay.

If a deal looks brilliant at first glance, add the parking before deciding whether it is still brilliant.

Families and accessibility

The hotel is family-friendly, with interconnecting room options and children's menus. Public areas have step-free access, adapted toilets and lifts to all floors. If you need a specific accessible-bedroom layout or shower arrangement, It is worth confirming that exact room with the hotel before booking.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 3.9 out of 5 from more than 7,700 reviews. That is a huge review base, which is useful because it gives you a much better picture than a handful of five-star comments.

The overall pattern is that people like the central location and convenience, while a score below 4 tells you not every stay is perfect. blackpool-fourrooms.guideContent:
FourRooms Blackpool · Reads Avenue

FourRooms is a completely different proposition from the big seafront hotels. This is a small, privately run Blackpool B&B with only four individually styled suites, so if you prefer somewhere personal rather than a 200-room hotel, this is the sort of place that stands out.

Only four rooms — and that is the point

The property is at 60 Reads Avenue, close to the town centre, promenade and Central Pier. The four suites are individually decorated rather than being rows of identical chain-hotel bedrooms.

The official site lists VisitEngland 5 Star Gold status along with breakfast and other awards, and the public feedback is unusually strong for Blackpool accommodation.

Breakfast matters here

This is not one of those places where breakfast is an afterthought. FourRooms has specifically held breakfast awards, and recent guest feedback repeatedly singles breakfast out as one of the best parts of the stay.

If breakfast is important to you, this is the sort of small property where the meal is part of the identity rather than just another buffet tray downstairs.

Parking and Wi-Fi

The official site advertises free parking and free Wi-Fi. Free parking is a genuine advantage around central Blackpool because a lot of larger hotels now charge per night.

Who runs it?

Recent guest reviews repeatedly name Paul and Michael as the hosts and describe a very hands-on welcome. That fits the whole FourRooms idea: this is a small hospitality business where the people looking after the property are a visible part of the stay.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows a perfect 5.0 out of 5 from more than 850 reviews and ranks it among Blackpool's strongest B&Bs and inns. That is an exceptional public-review record, especially over that many reviews.

The recurring praise is for cleanliness, attention to detail, breakfast and hospitality. With only four suites, availability is naturally going to be tighter than a large chain hotel, so this is one where booking early matters.

Where it sits for an arcade trip

Reads Avenue puts you within the central Blackpool area rather than out at the far north or south ends. Our own Blackpool directory includes Coral Island, Carousel Amusements, Happy Dayz, Pat's 10p Prize Bingo, Funland and many more around the central promenade, plus Arcade Club Blackpool and Tenpin away from the seafront.

That makes FourRooms useful if you want a quieter small-property base but still want to walk into the central entertainment area.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for this for couples and adults who prefer a small, highly rated B&B with breakfast and personal hosting over a large entertainment hotel. If you want a swimming pool, nightly cabaret and hundreds of rooms, this is the wrong category entirely.

Before booking

Check the exact suite, breakfast inclusion and cancellation terms. The official property says booking direct is cheaper than Booking.com, while our affiliate route may surface other partner rates. hayling-aff-zen-sinah-warren.guideContent:
Sinah Warren · Hayling Island

Sinah Warren is not a normal seaside hotel where you book a room and then spend the whole day trying to find things to do somewhere else. Warner has built the break around the hotel itself: food, entertainment, pools, activities and the coastal setting are all part of the reason you would stay here.

It is also adults-only, which immediately separates it from Hayling Island's family holiday parks.

Where it is

The hotel sits on Ferry Road on the south-west side of Hayling Island, overlooking Langstone Harbour. The setting is quieter and more resort-like than staying around the main seafront attractions.

The hotel describes the site as a coastal retreat with extensive grounds, sea views and access to the shoreline. Some accommodation has balconies or patios and there are both hotel rooms and garden chalets.

Breakfast and dinner are part of the break

This is one of the biggest differences compared with a basic room-only hotel. Warner states that breakfast and three-course evening dinner are included with breaks. Breakfast is designed as a proper leisurely meal, and evening dining rotates through familiar favourites, seasonal dishes and specials.

There are also lounges, bars, coffee and lighter daytime options. So if you are staying several nights, you are not expected to fend for yourself every evening.

Leisure facilities

Sinah Warren has a heated indoor pool, heated outdoor pool in season, sauna, steam room, fitness centre and spa treatment rooms. The outdoor pool normally operates from June into early September, while the indoor pool is available year-round.

Spa access is included with breaks, while individual beauty and spa treatments cost extra.

Entertainment and activities

Nightly entertainment is a major part of the Warner setup, with live music, tribute acts, bands, DJs and shows in the Late Lounge. During the day there are activities ranging from quizzes and bowls to aqua aerobics, archery, axe throwing, dancing, fitness sessions and cinema screenings. Some are included and others carry a supplement.

If you are the sort of person who hates a hotel where there is nothing to do after dinner, this is basically the opposite.

Accessibility and restrictions

Warner asks guests who need a fully accessible room to contact the hotel when booking so the correct accommodation can be matched. Service dogs are accepted. Children under 18 are not admitted because this is an adults-only Warner hotel.

What is nearby for our readers?

For a Spin Raiders trip, the main Hayling Island arcade stop is Funland Hayling Island Arcade on the seafront. Our directory also includes the arcade at Mill Rythe Holiday Village. Sinah Warren itself is on the quieter harbour side, so this is not a case of walking out of reception straight into the main arcade strip.

That can actually work well if you want a quieter base with proper evening entertainment, then drive or travel across the island for the traditional seaside part of the day.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for Sinah Warren for an adults-only coastal break where you want breakfast, dinner and entertainment bundled into the stay. It also suits people who actually use hotel leisure facilities rather than just looking at a photo of the swimming pool online and never going near it.

If you want children with you, this is not the property. If you want to be right on Hayling's amusement seafront, there are better-positioned choices. If you want a resort-style adult break with things happening inside the hotel, Sinah Warren makes much more sense.

eff27442-9f6a-459a-a98f-45cb6ad74ca5.guideContent:
Leonardo Hotel Leeds · Brewery Wharf

Leonardo Hotel Leeds is one of those city hotels where the location does a lot of the work for you. It sits at Brewery Wharf, close enough to walk into the centre without feeling as though you are sleeping right in the middle of the busiest shopping streets, and it also puts you on the right side of town for Leeds Dock and the Royal Armouries.

First thing to know: it is a proper city hotel, not just a room for the night

There are 248 rooms here, with standard doubles, double-and-single rooms, superior rooms, family options and executive rooms. The standard setup includes an en-suite bathroom, free Wi-Fi, a flat-screen television, work desk and tea and coffee facilities. Family rooms can take up to two adults and two children under twelve, while the executive rooms add a super-king bed and coffee machine.

That matters because some city-centre offers look cheap until you realise the hotel is really aimed at a quick overnight stop. Leonardo Leeds is set up for couples, families and longer business stays as well, with 24-hour reception, luggage storage and 24-hour room service if you get back late.

Breakfast is more than a pastry by reception

The breakfast setup is a proper hot-and-cold buffet. There are cooked items alongside cereals, pastries, fruit, tea, coffee and juice. On weekdays the continental breakfast starts at 6:30am and the hot breakfast from 7am, with both running to 9:30am. At weekends and on public holidays the service runs later, with continental from 7am and hot breakfast from 7:30am through to 11am.

A takeaway continental breakfast can also be requested. So if you are heading out early for a train, an event or a full day around Leeds, you are not automatically stuck missing breakfast.

You can eat here in the evening as well

The hotel has its own restaurant and bar rather than sending you straight back outside to find food. The current restaurant menu includes steaks, curries, salads and lighter protein dishes, with gluten-free choices and a children's menu. Dinner service is listed from 6pm to 9:30pm, while bar food runs from noon to 9:30pm.

That makes the hotel useful for two completely different sorts of stay. If you want to be out in Leeds all day and eat somewhere in the centre, there is no shortage of choice nearby. If you are knackered after travelling or you have dragged the family around attractions all day, you can simply eat at the hotel instead.

The parking needs reading before you set off

This is the bit It is useful to know before arriving with a car: there is not a big free hotel car park waiting underneath you. The hotel directs drivers to public parking nearby, including Brewery Wharf Tetley Car Park beside the hotel, and charges apply.

Parking is one of the recurring weaker points in public reviews, so do not leave it until you are sitting in traffic outside the hotel. Check the current recommended car park, price and walking route before leaving home. If the deal is cheap but parking adds a noticeable amount to the stay, you want to know that before clicking book, not afterwards.

Accessibility and family use

The hotel describes itself as disabled-friendly. There are wheelchair-accessible rooms with wider doorways and additional space, lifts serve the rooms, and family rooms are available. If you need a particular shower arrangement, turning space, bed height or other specific adaptation, It is still worth contact the hotel before booking so check the latest details every accessible room is identical.

Guide dogs are accepted; other pets are not.

What current guests are actually saying

At the time of this check, Google shows the hotel at 4.0 out of 5 from more than 2,400 reviews, while Tripadvisor is also showing 4.0 out of 5 from more than 3,300 reviews. The strongest recurring point is the location. Cleanliness and service are generally rated positively as well, and breakfast gets plenty of praise.

The criticism is worth knowing too. Some recent reviewers describe parts of the bedrooms and bathrooms as dated or tired, and parking comes up repeatedly as something guests would like explained more clearly. There are also mixed comments around air-conditioning and room condition. So It is worth not sell this as some flawless luxury hotel because the guide pattern does not support that. What it looks like is a very well-positioned four-star city base where the location, breakfast and staff are doing a lot of the heavy lifting, while some rooms may feel more worn than the glossy photos suggest.

For Spin Raiders readers, the Leeds location is actually useful

This is where the hotel starts making more sense for our sort of trip. The Royal Armouries Museum is roughly an eight-minute walk away according to current Google hotel-location information, so you have a proper attraction practically on the doorstep.

Our Leeds directory also has plenty if you want gaming or entertainment built into the trip. In the city you can find NQ64 Leeds for an arcade-bar night, Tenpin Leeds for bowling and arcade games, Storey Group on Call Lane, Royal Amusements on Kirkgate, MERKUR on New York Street, plus Funstation and Carousel at The Light. Further out you have Arcade Club Leeds and Hollywood Bowl.

That means this is not a hotel where you arrive, sleep and wonder what to do. You can turn it into a proper Leeds day out: Royal Armouries, food around the centre, an arcade or bowling session, then back to Brewery Wharf without needing to build the entire day around the car.

Train travel is straightforward

Leonardo lists Leeds station at around a ten-minute walk, while current Google location data puts it at roughly twelve to thirteen minutes on foot depending on route. That makes the hotel particularly useful if you are coming in by train and do not want the cost or hassle of city-centre parking at all.

This works well for Leonardo Leeds if you want a central base for a couple's break, an event, a family day out or a Leeds arcade run and you would rather walk into the city than keep moving the car around. It also makes sense for train travel because of the station distance.

If your priority is a brand-new boutique bedroom or free on-site parking, read the latest room reviews carefully because those are the two areas where expectations could get ahead of reality.

c7cdf853-ad57-4b3d-94f1-5e7b28eb34d8.guideContent:
The Corona Hotel Blackpool · South Beach

The Corona is one of those Blackpool places where the story is part of the appeal. It is an original Art Deco hotel built in 1936, sitting in the quieter South Beach area just off the main seafront and only minutes from Pleasure Beach, Sandcastle Waterpark and South Pier.

Independent and hands-on

The current owners say they have operated The Corona since August 2001 and take a very hands-on role. They describe themselves meeting guests, cooking and serving breakfast and dinner, working the bar and getting involved in housekeeping.

That tells you immediately this is not a franchise hotel run from a head office. It is a smaller independent business with 22 en-suite rooms.

The rooms

There are solo, twin, double and superior rooms, with superior options offering king-size beds and extra amenities. All rooms have en-suite shower rooms, Elemis toiletries and free Wi-Fi.

Breakfast and food

Breakfast is included on direct bookings unless you deliberately choose a room-only rate. That distinction matters because third-party packages can have different inclusions, so never assume the affiliate price automatically includes breakfast just because the hotel's direct rate does.

The owners also describe themselves serving dinner and working the bar, so this is more than a room-only guest house. If you are staying several nights, check the current dinner availability and whether it is included or separately charged for your dates.

Parking

The hotel says free parking is available on and off site, with limited allocated parking for some direct bookings. If parking is important, ring before arrival because 'free parking' and 'guaranteed space outside the door' are not the same thing.

Family use and pets

The Corona describes itself as family-friendly. Small dogs can be accepted, but only when arranged by phone. The hotel does not accept stag or hen groups, which is useful to know if you are choosing somewhere quieter in South Beach.

Location for the Blackpool day out

This is where the hotel is strong. You are close to Pleasure Beach, Sandcastle and South Pier rather than having to cross the whole resort every time you want the South Shore attractions.

For arcades, our directory includes the Main Arcade and Playdium around Pleasure Beach, Grosvenor Casino on South Promenade, plus Coral Island, Carousel Amusements, Funland and the central promenade arcades further north.

Guest feedback

The hotel currently has a very strong public reputation, with the existing Spin Raiders record showing 4.9 from hundreds of reviews. That does not remove the need to read recent comments, but it is a very different review picture from some of Blackpool's much larger hotels.

The current offer

The Wowcher-linked package on Spin Raiders currently includes breakfast, prosecco and late checkout on selected dates, with other upgrades depending on the package. Because the hotel itself has different direct-booking inclusions, compare the actual package carefully before paying.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for The Corona if you want South Beach, an independent owner-run hotel, breakfast as part of the stay and a quieter base close to Pleasure Beach. If you want a massive entertainment hotel with a pool and cabaret every night, there are other Blackpool properties built more around that.

Before booking

Check breakfast, parking, pet arrangements if needed, minimum-stay rules and the exact room category. Spin Raiders may earn commission from qualifying affiliate bookings, at no extra cost to you.

wowcher_blackpool_imperial_2026.guideContent:
The Imperial Hotel Blackpool · North Promenade

The Imperial is one of those Blackpool hotels you know before you have even stayed there. Big Victorian seafront building, North Promenade position, trams outside and enough history that it feels very different from a generic chain box dropped beside a retail park.

Location

The hotel sits directly on the Promenade, north of the busiest central strip. That means you still have the seafront and tram connection but you are not sleeping on top of Coral Island or the Central Pier crowds.

For some people that is ideal: quieter base, then tram or walk down to the action. If you want to step out of the hotel and immediately be surrounded by arcades, choose something further south.

Food and current packages

The Imperial is operating much more like a destination hotel than a bare room-only base. Current packages include breakfast and, on some offers, dinner and entertainment. The hotel's own family-break information is now pushing all-inclusive style packages with meals, activities and extras bundled together.

The affiliate deal attached to this guide currently includes breakfast, late checkout and live entertainment, with a dinner upgrade on selected dates. Always check the final package because the exact meal plan changes between offers.

Parking

The hotel has parking, but it is charged. From January 2026 the hotel lists parking at £14 per car per 24 hours. Put that into your comparison straight away because three nights adds another £42 before you have spent anything in Blackpool.

Guest feedback

Read recent guest reviews for your chosen room type before booking, paying attention to room condition, service and noise. Ratings and review counts change, so check the current Tripadvisor listing alongside the room description and booking terms.

That is the point of a Spin Raiders guide: show the deal, but also show the bit that helps you decide whether the building and current standards suit you.

Blackpool is where this hotel becomes easy to use

Our Blackpool directory is packed. You have Coral Island Casino, Carousel Amusements, Happy Dayz, Funland, Pat's 10p Prize Bingo, Arcade Club Blackpool, Tenpin, Pleasure Beach arcades, Grosvenor Casino and Genting, plus many more further along the promenade.

The tram is useful from North Promenade because you can move along the seafront without shifting the car every time. That is particularly handy if your day is basically a run of arcades, piers, food and attractions.

Who this hotel suits

This is a strong option for The Imperial if you want the old Blackpool hotel feel, a seafront base, entertainment and the option of meal-inclusive packages. Do not choose it automatically just because it says four-star: with a historic hotel this size, read the newest room reviews and compare the exact room grade.

Before you book

aee87420-6662-4c94-bb40-1bef94640ca4.guideContent:
The Lyndene Hotel · Blackpool Promenade

The Lyndene is not trying to be a quiet boutique hotel where everybody whispers in the lounge. Its whole identity is Blackpool entertainment: seafront position, bars, restaurants and live acts every day of the year.

If that is what you want, brilliant. If you want to be in bed at half nine with absolute silence, this probably is not the first Blackpool hotel It is worth point you towards.

The entertainment is the headline

The hotel advertises live entertainment 365 days a year and can run several cabaret, tribute and speciality acts in one night. There are themed events and daytime entertainment as well.

That means your evening does not necessarily end when you come back from the promenade. For plenty of Blackpool visitors, that is exactly the point of staying here.

Food

The hotel has multiple dining and lounge spaces. The current affiliate package attached to this page includes a three-course dinner on the first night, full English breakfast and nightly live entertainment, with a midday checkout.

For a multi-night stay, check whether dinner is included beyond the first night or whether you will be paying separately, because package wording matters.

Parking and Wi-Fi

The Lyndene advertises free parking and free Wi-Fi. Free parking is a real advantage in Blackpool because several large seafront hotels charge per night. As with any limited hotel car park, It is worth confirming the current arrangement if parking is essential to your trip.

Guest feedback

Tripadvisor currently shows 3.8 out of 5 from about 3,100 reviews. The entertainment and seafront position are major positives, but the overall score also tells you experiences are not universally five-star.

On a hotel this focused on live entertainment, your enjoyment is going to depend heavily on whether that atmosphere is what you came for. It is worth read the newest comments on bedrooms, food and noise before booking.

For an arcade-heavy Blackpool trip

The position works. Our directory has Carousel Amusements, Coral Island, Happy Dayz, Funland, Pat's 10p Prize Bingo and plenty more along the central promenade, while Arcade Club and Tenpin give you alternatives away from the traditional seafront arcades.

You can easily make the hotel the base for a full day of arcades and then come back for the evening entertainment rather than having to find another show or bar afterwards.

Who this hotel suits

This works well for The Lyndene for couples and adults who actually want Blackpool-style live entertainment built into the hotel stay. It also makes sense if free parking is important.

It may be less suitable if you want a quiet early night or you are choosing purely on star rating rather than atmosphere.
